text:
Maya K.: Quick sync — I'm proposing we standardize internal RPC on gRPC + protobufs, and put a small gateway that transcodes JSON for the Console and external clients. Main open concerns: quotas attribution, error schemas, telemetry propagation, and safe rollout/rollback paths. Thoughts?

Nikhil: +1 on gRPC for latency/cpu. Big question: how do product teams call endpoints during migration? will we support dual-stack endpoints? :thinking: 

Sara: Dual-stack seems required for a while. Also worried about losing auth/claims when transcoding. We rely on structured auth metadata for quota and billing.

Dave: We can forward a compact claim blob in a single header rather than many headers. e.g.
```
x-rd-claims: eyJpZCI6IjEwMDIiLCJ0IjoiYXBwIn0=\n
```
Then gateway decodes and applies per-route checks. But watch header size.

Emily: Console UX needs stable JSON error shapes. gRPC statuses != our JSON error model. Gateway should normalize errors into {"code":"...","message":"...","details":{}} so frontend logic doesn't change.

Maya K.: Rollout idea: start with read-only routes mapped to new proto first. Canary 5% traffic -> validate quotas, errors, traces for 24h -> bump. Failover: gateway returns 502 -> clients automatically hit legacy endpoint (we already have a fallback router). Need SLO checks to trigger rollback.

Nikhil: Also ensure quota attribution: tokens or api-key must map 1:1 across translation. If gateway mints a different internal caller id we'll break billing.

Sara: Telemetry: traceparent needs to survive. Envoy-based transcode should preserve W3C traceparent or inject x-cloud-trace-context. Minimal example:
```
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
```
If traces drop at the gateway we lose request-level debug info.

deploy-bot: canary deployed: rfc-proto-gateway v0.1 -> cluster-a (5%) by maya-k at 4132134700

infra-bot: FYI ALB header limit ~8KB, nginx default header buffer smaller. If claims approach gets big we need a session-store or short claim id.

Dave: Practical fallback: put claim blob in a short id header and store blob in redis keyed by id. Gateway reads id -> fetch claims. Adds one extra lookup but keeps headers small.

Maya K.: Good point. For MVP let's: 1) prototype claim-blob header (base64) for small payloads, 2) implement redis mapping for larger payloads, 3) gateway normalizes errors, 4) preserve traceparent. I'll write the integration spec and a rollout playbook with canary checks (quota match, error rate, trace continuity).

Emily: Can you add acceptance criteria for console team? e.g., identical JSON schema + stable status codes + no UI diffs on canary.

Maya K.: Yup—I'll add that. I'll ping console/product and schedule a short spike pairing session tomorrow. If anyone has an absolute blocker speak up now.

Sara: No blockers from infra. Need doc about jwt claim encoding though.

Nikhil: I'll write the quota mapping table (old caller-id -> new internal principal) and share.

Maya K.: Thanks all. I'll post the spec in #eng-platform and raise a lightweight RFC. :thumbsup:
